item.content:encoded:
Window: 15 Oct 10:00 → 15 Oct 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Drupal Patches Critical Core RCE Flaw with No-Login Path via Contributed Modules — Must Read

Drupal released critical security updates for a Field UI remote code execution flaw (CVE-2026-108097) that contributed modules or custom code can expose without login. Sites should upgrade to supported fixed releases immediately or temporarily uninstall Field UI; the Entity List module requires a separate update for a similar RCE flaw.

  • Drupal released updates on October 14 for CVE-2026-108097, a critical Field UI flaw that can allow code execution on a site server through contributed modules or custom code.
  • The advisory states that Drupal core alone does not provide a path to the flaw, but at least one known contributed-module path does not require a login.
  • Affected supported branches should update to Drupal 11.4.10, 11.3.19, or 10.6.19, while sites unable to update can temporarily uninstall the Field UI module.
  • Drupal also issued a separate critical advisory for the Entity List module, CVE-2026-108099, and updating Drupal core does not update that module.
  • The same Drupal core releases fix two moderately critical cross-site scripting flaws in the Link and Navigation modules that require at least a logged-in user.

Technologies: cms, waf

Products: drupal-core, field-ui, entity-list, drupal-steward

Vendors: drupal, pantheon, acquia

ADINT: Weaponized Ad Tech for Zero-Click Spyware and Mass Identity Vacuuming — Must Read

Confiant found that Discover-Tech allegedly weaponized its large ad-tech footprint to collect cookies and device identities at internet scale, then selectively deliver encrypted, remotely controlled JavaScript through infrastructure attributed by Citizen Lab to Candiru. The operation appears designed for stealthy ADINT surveillance and potential zero-click spyware staging rather than ordinary advertising or financially motivated malvertising.

  • Confiant reported that Discover-Tech’s ad-serving infrastructure delivered encrypted JavaScript through small hidden frames and handed some traffic to CloudFront infrastructure that Citizen Lab attributed to Candiru.
  • The analyzed JavaScript fingerprinted devices and network capabilities, monitored user interactions, contacted a command server for instructions, and could decrypt and execute code supplied by the operator.
  • Confiant observed Discover-Tech ad code sending browser cookies, high-detail browser and device information, and other identity fields to Discover-Tech-controlled endpoints; on shared publisher pages, this could include non-HttpOnly first-party cookies.
  • Confiant estimated that Discover-Tech served roughly 10 million ad impressions per day and said its cookie-matching infrastructure generated billions of audience touch-points per month across tens of thousands of websites.
  • Discover-Tech ads were observed in 228 countries and on networks associated with government, research, education, health, defense, judicial, security, and international organizations.

Technologies: cloud-platform, object-storage, load-balancer

Products: mtrtb, trustlayersdk, cloudfront, amazon-s3, elastic-load-balancing, myipinfo

Vendors: discover-tech, candiru, intelos, amazon-web-services, cloudflare

Inside Help TDS: Hotejka, Cloudflare Pages, and Predictive Detection — Should Read

Infoblox links the long-running Help TDS tech-support-scam operation to the Russian-language Hotejka/ROI777 affiliate program, which routes traffic from compromised sites, spam, and ads into browser-lock scams that persuade victims to install remote-access software. The group uses thousands of disposable Cloudflare Pages domains, but Infoblox says it can now predict many of those domains roughly seven days before they are deployed.

  • Infoblox assesses that the Russian-language Hotejka affiliate program operates Help TDS and is a rebrand of the previously exposed ROI777 operation.
  • Help TDS directs traffic from sources including compromised websites, malvertising, social-media posts, and spam to fake Microsoft browser-lock pages that prompt users to call scam call centers.
  • During a recorded call-center interaction, an operator claiming to be Microsoft Technical Support instructed the researchers to download UltraViewer remote desktop software.
  • Since April 2026, Help TDS has used free Cloudflare Pages sites and announced nearly 300 new Cloudflare Pages domains daily through a Telegram channel.
  • Infoblox reported detecting likely Help TDS Cloudflare Pages domains about seven days before their use and identified more than 16,000 domains later used for the TDS through mid-September.

Technologies: cloud-platform, remote-access, antivirus, cms

Products: infoblox-threat-defense, cloudflare-pages, ultraviewer, windows-defender, wordpress, keitaro

Vendors: infoblox, cloudflare, microsoft, automattic, keitaro

The Trello Invite Whose Subject Line the Attacker Wrote — Should Read

An attacker used a genuine Trello invitation, authenticated by Trello’s SPF, DKIM, and DMARC controls, to impersonate a bank CEO through attacker-controlled display-name and board-title fields. Defenders should inspect the platform-displayed inviter email address in the message body, not just the legitimate SaaS sender address.

  • An attacker created a Trello account using a Proton Mail address, set its display name to resemble a digital bank’s CEO, and created a board with an urgent compliance-themed title.
  • Trello sent the invitation from its legitimate infrastructure, and the message passed SPF, DKIM, and DMARC checks for trello.com.
  • The invitation body displayed the Proton Mail address of the actual Trello inviter alongside the impersonated executive name.
  • All links in the message pointed to Trello, Atlassian identity, tracking, or social-media pages, and the article reports no attachment, QR code, or confirmed board contents.
  • The article recommends treating SaaS notification display names and titles as attacker-controlled content and verifying the platform-displayed inviter address.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform

Products: trello, amazon-ses, gmail, ironscales

Vendors: atlassian, proton, amazon, google, ironscales

India Mandates Registered Caller Name Display on 4G and Newer Networks From November 1 — Should Read

India will require telecom providers to display the registered name associated with incoming domestic calls on 4G and newer networks starting November 1, 2026, to help combat spam and fraud. The name will come from carrier subscriber records when the number is not saved in the recipient’s contacts, while international calls will be labeled accordingly.

  • India has directed telecom service providers to display callers’ registered names alongside incoming phone numbers on 4G and newer networks starting November 1, 2026.
  • For numbers not saved in a recipient’s contacts, domestic calls will display the caller name recorded in the originating telecom provider’s subscriber database, while calls from outside India will be labeled “International Call.”
  • The Calling Name Presentation rollout does not yet cover 2G, 3G, or public switched telephone networks, which will be considered separately.
  • Telecom providers must maintain subscriber name-to-number databases, support efficient name queries, avoid retaining the caller name after an incoming call ends, and provide an option for callers to hide their identity.
  • Business or bulk-connection users may use a preferred name if it is a registered trademark or a trade name registered on the Goods and Services Tax portal.

Microsoft: Windows Server 2022 reached end of mainstream support — May Read

Windows Server 2022 reached end of mainstream support on October 13, 2026, but will continue receiving free monthly security updates under extended support through October 14, 2031. Microsoft recommends planning an upgrade to Windows Server 2025 for full mainstream support.

  • Windows Server 2022 reached the end of mainstream support on October 13, 2026, and its October 2026 security update was the last mainstream-support update.
  • Windows Server 2022 will receive free monthly security updates during extended support through October 14, 2031.
  • Microsoft extended hotpatching for Windows Server 2022 Datacenter: Azure Edition through October 2027.
  • Microsoft recommends that administrators plan an upgrade to Windows Server 2025, which has mainstream support until November 2029 and extended support until November 14, 2034.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows-server-2022, windows-server-2025, windows-11-24h2, windows-11-26h2

Vendors: microsoft

Police arrests 95 suspects in international CSAM crackdown action — May Read

An INTERPOL-coordinated operation across 17 Latin American and European countries arrested 95 suspects accused of distributing child sexual abuse material through online messaging groups. Investigators executed 127 search warrants, rescued a five-year-old victim, and expect seized evidence to identify more offenders and children at risk.

  • An INTERPOL-coordinated operation involving authorities from 17 countries in Latin America and Europe arrested 95 suspects accused of distributing child sexual abuse material through online messaging groups.
  • International Effort Confluencia included four law enforcement operations between March and September 2026, during which investigators executed 127 search warrants.
  • Authorities rescued a five-year-old victim whose parent had allegedly been producing and selling child sexual abuse material online.
  • Ecuadorian authorities found a suspected group member with about 15GB of abuse images and more than 4,000 files, while Panamanian investigators arrested an administrator of a group with more than 700 users.
  • INTERPOL said that material seized in the investigation is expected to help identify additional offenders and children at risk.

Silent Push 6.1 Enhances Brand and Infrastructure Impersonation — May Read

Silent Push 6.1 adds automated brand and infrastructure impersonation detection to identify and prioritize look-alike domains before they are used in phishing campaigns. The release also expands analyst workflows through XSOAR, browser, AI/MCP, and bidirectional TAXII integrations.

  • Silent Push launched version 6.1 of its preemptive cyber defense platform with a rebuilt, automated Brand and Infrastructure Impersonation capability.
  • The new impersonation engine continuously identifies look-alike domains, assigns risk scores, adds registrar and hosting information, groups related activity by threat actor, and exports evidence for takedown efforts.
  • Silent Push 6.1 adds investigation features including expanded searches for domains, IP addresses, ASNs, subnets, and HTML titles, along with passive DNS timelines and certificate information.
  • The release integrates Silent Push intelligence with Palo Alto Cortex XSOAR, a Chrome extension, AI assistants through an MCP server, and bidirectional threat-intelligence sharing through its updated TAXII server.
  • The interface is now available in Korean and Spanish as well as English, with Japanese planned shortly.

Technologies: soar, browser

Products: silent-push-6-1, cortex-xsoar, silent-push-chrome-extension, silent-push-mcp-server, silent-push-taxii-server

Vendors: silent-push, palo-alto-networks

AI Security Starts with Visibility Into Your SaaS Environment — Optional

AI security in SaaS starts with visibility into every agent’s owner, identity, data access, connected tools, and permitted actions. Apply least privilege, Zero Trust, continuous monitoring, and runtime safeguards such as prompt-injection defenses and approvals for high-impact actions.

  • AI agents in SaaS applications may act through a user’s access or through a service account, allowing them to retrieve documents, change records, call connected tools, or trigger workflows.
  • An effective AI-agent inventory should identify each agent’s business owner, intended task, access identity, reachable data, permitted actions, connected tools, and available activity records.
  • Organizations should apply least privilege by limiting an agent’s access to the specific data and actions needed for its assigned task, including reviewing the service accounts and repositories it uses.
  • For high-impact actions such as changing access settings or sending sensitive information outside the organization, teams should consider requiring explicit human approval.
  • AI agents can be manipulated by malicious instructions embedded in documents or support tickets, so workflows may need input checks, output inspection, restricted tools, and a tested process to pause or revoke access.

Technologies: casb, iam

Products: now-assist, agentguard, marlin-ai, ai-agent-inventory

Vendors: appomni, servicenow

Why AI Confidence Is Not Validation — Optional

AI-generated findings in digital forensics and incident response are not validation: practitioners must independently verify evidence, document the exact tools and versions used, and retain human authority over irreversible or legally consequential actions. SANS advocates separate AI governance frameworks for forensics and incident response because their speed and evidentiary-risk requirements differ.

  • AI confidence scores do not validate investigative findings, which must be independently confirmed against the original source files and evidence.
  • SANS created separate Digital Forensics & AI Investigations and Incident Response & AI Investigations frameworks, mapped respectively to SWGDE standards and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0.
  • Investigators should document the tool that produced an AI-assisted finding, and record the precise version when using a general-purpose model because capabilities change over time.
  • Incident response can allow more AI-assisted speed during active events when tools have been built and validated, while digital forensics requires validation of every source file.
  • AI should not make irreversible decisions such as collecting cloud data, choosing an acquisition approach, or deploying tools to capture activity across systems; human practitioners remain responsible for those choices.

Products: digital-forensics-ai-investigations-framework, incident-response-ai-investigations-framework, for498, for508, for608

Vendors: sans-institute

Reverse proof of work: How AI changed hiring signals — Optional

AI has made polished take-home assignments and codebase analyses cheap to produce but costly to verify, weakening them as hiring signals. Hiring processes should focus less on volume and more on candidates’ demonstrated judgment, validation, prioritization, and reasoning.

  • The author views hiring as an information problem in which each interview step should reduce a specific uncertainty about the candidate and the role.
  • Traditional hiring signals such as take-home assignments can be useful because they are difficult for candidates to produce but relatively quick for employers to review.
  • AI can make long technical analyses cheap to produce while leaving employers with the expensive task of validating claims and deciding what the work reveals about the candidate.
  • The author calls this shift “reverse proof of work,” where production is inexpensive but verification remains costly.
  • The article argues that hiring processes should reward judgment, prioritization, validation, and explanation of trade-offs rather than the volume of material a candidate produces.

Vendors: castle

Fake AI Attacks Spread Across US Companies: How MSSPs Can Stop Incidents Early — Optional

Attackers are impersonating popular AI services such as Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini to trick employees into running PowerShell-based malware that can steal browser sessions and business credentials. The article promotes behavioral sandboxing and threat-intelligence sharing as ways for MSSPs to detect related campaigns faster across clients.

  • ANY.RUN linked 1,258 public sandbox analyses to fake AI campaigns between April and October 2026, with 16% of country-attributed targets located in the United States.
  • The campaigns impersonate AI brands including Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini through sponsored search results, legitimate hosting services, shared AI conversations, and counterfeit download sites.
  • In an analyzed fake Claude download campaign, clicking a Windows download button copied a command that launched mshta.exe, retrieved a malicious HTA file, and initiated an encoded PowerShell execution chain.
  • ANY.RUN states that its Interactive Sandbox enables analysts to reproduce suspicious interactions in isolation and observe resulting processes, network activity, and malicious behavior.
  • The article says MSSPs can reuse investigation findings and threat-intelligence indicators across customer environments to improve detection, triage, and threat hunting.

Products: any-run-interactive-sandbox, any-run-threat-intelligence-feeds, any-run-threat-intelligence-lookup, claude, chatgpt, github-copilot, gemini

Vendors: any-run, anthropic, openai, github, google

Predictive Security Starts With What Threat Actors Already Have — Optional

Constella promotes predictive security as a way to use breached and infostealer-derived identity data alongside internal access context to identify and remediate likely attack paths before intrusion is detected. The approach prioritizes actions such as credential resets, session reviews, device investigation, and monitoring for exposed high-risk accounts.

  • Predictive security uses evidence about threats, exposures, and business context to identify likely attack paths and support action before attackers exploit them.
  • Constella Intelligence says it analyzes breach data and infostealer logs to identify compromised identities, stolen credentials, and related connections.
  • Organizations can combine external exposure intelligence with internal details such as account status, access privileges, authentication controls, and business impact to prioritize responses.
  • In the article’s illustrative scenario, a security team responds to exposed employee credentials by investigating the device, resetting credentials, reviewing active sessions, and examining recent account activity.
  • The article recommends measuring time from exposure alert to assessment, time from validation to remediation, unresolved high-priority exposures, and repeated exposure involving the same identities.

Vendors: constella-intelligence

item.title: Actively Exploited PAN-OS and AhsayCBS Flaws Lead Security Updates
item.content:encoded:
Window: 15 Oct 06:00 → 15 Oct 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

Langflow's Critical Authenticated RCE Flaw Targeted in 1,423 Honeypot Exploit Attempts — Must Read

Attackers are actively targeting CVE-2026-105740, a critical authenticated RCE flaw in Langflow versions before 1.9.0 that lets any authenticated user execute arbitrary server commands through malicious MCP server configurations. Organizations should upgrade immediately, disable auto-login, enforce strong credentials, and investigate suspicious requests to Langflow MCP endpoints.

  • CVE-2026-105740 is a critical authenticated remote-code-execution flaw, rated 9.9 out of 10, affecting Langflow versions before 1.9.0.
  • The flaw allows any authenticated Langflow user, including a non-administrator, to run arbitrary operating-system commands by creating an MCP server configuration with the stdio transport and then fetching the server list.
  • Previdian recorded 1,423 exploit attempts from 27 attacker IP addresses against its honeypot sensors since September 19, 2026, with activity rising to 333 attempts on October 11.
  • Observed payloads attempted to collect Langflow environment variables and secret settings, access the host filesystem through Docker commands, and run basic commands such as id and whoami.
  • Langflow and Previdian recommend upgrading to a patched version, disabling auto-login, using strong unique passwords, restricting access to trusted users, and reviewing requests to the MCP server endpoints.

Products: langflow

Vendors: langflow, datastax, ibm, previdian, greynoise

Palo Alto Networks Patches PAN-OS Authenticated RCE Flaw Amid Active Exploitation — Must Read

Palo Alto Networks has patched CVE-2026-0322, an actively exploited authenticated PAN-OS management-interface flaw that lets attackers execute code as root on affected PA-Series, VM-Series, and Panorama systems. Organizations should urgently update to fixed releases and restrict management access to trusted internal addresses or a jump box.

  • Palo Alto Networks released security updates for CVE-2026-0322, a high-severity PAN-OS management-interface flaw that is under active exploitation.
  • CVE-2026-0322 allows an authenticated attacker with network access to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on affected firewalls.
  • The issue affects PAN-OS on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and Panorama virtual and M-Series systems, while Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not affected.
  • Palo Alto Networks said it has observed very limited exploitation and listed three U.S.-geolocated IP addresses assessed to be linked to exploit attempts.
  • CISA added CVE-2026-0322 and Cisco Secure Email Gateway flaw CVE-2026-76519 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

Technologies: firewall, email-security, cloud-platform

Products: pan-os, pa-series, vm-series, panorama, cloud-ngfw, prisma-access, cisco-secure-email-gateway

Vendors: palo-alto-networks, cisco

AhsayCBS Flaws Exploited to Deploy Web Shells Get New Fixes After Incomplete Patches — Must Read

Ahsay Backup released new AhsayCBS hotfixes after earlier patches failed to fully fix two actively exploited flaws that attackers chained to gain unauthenticated remote code execution and install web shells and XMRig miners. Organizations should upgrade to AhsayCBS 10.3.4.45 or 9.15.2.70 and reboot affected servers.

  • Ahsay Backup released new AhsayCBS hotfixes for CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134 after earlier patches did not completely fix the flaws.
  • Attackers have chained the two flaws to bypass authentication, run arbitrary commands, and deploy web shells and XMRig cryptocurrency miners on exposed systems.
  • The new fixes are available in AhsayCBS version 10.3.4.45 hotfix and version 9.15.2.70 hotfix, and Ahsay says servers should be rebooted after installation.
  • Huntress independently verified that the AhsayCBS 10.3.4.45 hotfix mitigates the initial entry point used in the attack chain.
  • CISA added the two vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and required U.S. federal agencies to apply patches by October 17, 2026.

Technologies: backup

Products: ahsaycbs

Vendors: ahsay-backup, huntress

GhostAction Compromises About 1,900 GitHub Accounts, Targets Over 30,000 Repositories — Must Read

GhostAction attackers compromised about 1,900 GitHub accounts and pushed malicious GitHub Actions workflows to more than 30,000 repositories to steal CI/CD secrets, cloud credentials, and package registry tokens. GitHub began blocking the workflows on October 9, limiting later waves, but previously exposed secrets may remain at risk if they were not rotated.

  • GhostAction targeted more than 30,000 GitHub repositories across 3,000 users and organizations during activity observed on October 8 and 9, 2026.
  • The campaign compromised about 1,900 GitHub accounts and attempted to extract 3,174 secrets from public repositories’ automated build and deployment processes.
  • Attackers used stolen personal access tokens or credentials from information-stealing logs and dumps to gain repository write access and add malicious GitHub Actions workflow files.
  • The malicious workflows sought cloud credentials, software package registry tokens, AI provider API keys, and secrets found in repository history.
  • GitHub began preventing the malicious workflow from running on October 9, so later waves observed on October 10 and 12 could not extract secrets.

Technologies: ci-cd, source-control, cloud-platform, package-registry

Products: github-actions, github, gitlab, aws, npm, pypi, docker-hub

Vendors: github, gitguardian, gitlab, amazon-web-services, npm, pypi, docker

UK Legal Aid Agency: Hackers stole records dating back to 1978 — Should Read

The UK Legal Aid Agency says attackers who breached its systems in April 2025 stole sensitive legal-aid records dating as far back as 1978, including roughly 250,000 records from before 2007. The agency says there is no evidence the exfiltrated personal data has been published and is increasing investment in system modernization and cybersecurity.

  • The UK Legal Aid Agency said attackers who breached its IT systems in April 2025 stole records with an earliest verified date of 1978.
  • Most of the stolen data concerns legal-aid applications, claims, payments, or live cases from January 2007 to 16 May 2025, while approximately 250,000 records predate 2007.
  • The stolen information may include applicants’ contact details, dates of birth, national ID numbers, criminal histories, employment status, and financial contribution, debt, and payment details.
  • Data belonging to legal-aid providers was also taken, including contracts, office locations, financial and contact information, and LAA Online Portal credentials.
  • The Ministry of Justice said there is currently no evidence that the personal data believed to have been taken has been published and that it is investing more than £200 million in modernizing legal-aid digital services and cyber security.

Products: laa-online-portal

Vendors: legal-aid-agency

The GhostX Ecosystem: Forged in Transit, Licensed to Deceive — Should Read

Cyble uncovered GhostX, an active ecosystem distributing GhostBat RAT through fake Indian mParivahan and eChallan apps, with backend infrastructure for phishing, device management, and campaign control. The latest Android malware abuses Accessibility Services to stealthily capture PINs in Google Pay, MobiKwik, and dozens of other financial apps while dynamically changing its C2 and features through Firebase.

  • Cyble identified GhostX as an operator-controlled ecosystem linking phishing sites, Firebase-based backend services, device management, and distribution of GhostBat RAT through fake mParivahan and eChallan Android apps.
  • GhostBat RAT is distributed through text-message phishing campaigns that direct victims to fake transport-service or Google Play-style pages hosting malicious APK files, including assets hosted on GitHub.
  • The latest GhostBat RAT variant abuses Android Accessibility Service to place transparent touch regions over Google Pay and MobiKwik PIN keypads, capture the selected digits, and replay the taps into the genuine app.
  • The malware also uses accessibility events to capture PIN-like input from 60 targeted Indian banking, UPI, wallet, fintech, and payment applications.
  • Firebase Remote Config lets the operators change GhostBat RAT’s command-and-control backend and selectively enable or disable malware functions without redistributing the APK.

Technologies: mobile-os, cloud-platform, source-control

Products: android, google-pay, mobikwik, firebase-remote-config, firebase-cloud-messaging, github

Vendors: google, mobikwik, github

Microsoft fixes bug causing Windows black screens, Explorer crashes — May Read

Microsoft fixed a Windows 11 issue causing black screens, desktop-loading failures, and Explorer crashes, primarily affecting Azure Virtual Desktop hosts using FSLogix. Installing cumulative updates released on or after October 13, 2026 resolves the problem.

  • Microsoft resolved a Windows 11 issue that caused black screens after sign-in, desktop-loading problems, and Windows Explorer crashes.
  • The issue mainly affected Azure Virtual Desktop hosts using FSLogix, which is used to speed up user profile loading in virtual desktop environments.
  • Windows updates released on or after October 13, 2026, resolve the issue, according to Microsoft.
  • Users unable to install the latest updates can temporarily start Windows Explorer manually through Task Manager by running explorer.exe.
  • Enterprise-managed devices can use Microsoft’s Known Issue Rollback group policies for Windows 11 versions 26H1, 25H2, and 24H2 until they deploy the permanent update.

Palo Alto Networks warns of PAN-OS RCE flaw exploited in attacks — Must Read

Palo Alto Networks patched CVE-2026-0322, a high-severity PAN-OS management-interface flaw that allows authenticated attackers with network access to execute code as root and has already seen limited exploitation. Organizations should urgently update affected firewalls and restrict management-interface access to trusted internal IP addresses.

  • Palo Alto Networks released security updates for CVE-2026-0322, a PAN-OS management-interface flaw with a severity score of 8.6 that can allow authenticated attackers with network access to run code as root.
  • Palo Alto Networks said it has observed very limited exploitation of CVE-2026-0322 targeting management interfaces.
  • Affected products include PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and Panorama virtual and M-Series appliances, while Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not affected.

Unit 42 Uncovers PEERSTITCH, a Stealthy FortiGate Implant — Must Read

Unit 42 found that attackers exploited a FortiManager flaw to steal configurations, credentials, and trust material for more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls, then used that access for traffic sniffing, VPN access, and management impersonation. They also deployed PEERSTITCH, a memory-resident FortiOS implant that patches core processes and evades conventional disk- and network-based detection.

  • Unit 42 investigated a September 2024 intrusion against a telecommunications managed service provider tracked as CL-STA-0954, also known as UNC5820.
  • The attackers exploited CVE-2024-47575 on a FortiManager appliance and exfiltrated an archive containing configurations, credential material, cryptographic keys, and information on more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls.
  • The attackers pushed unauthorized packet-capture configurations to managed FortiGate devices to collect unencrypted HTTP traffic and traffic associated with targeted services, including TFTP, RADIUS, and LDAP.
  • By exploiting CVE-2025-61624, the attackers deployed PEERSTITCH, an ARM64 implant that patches the memory of FortiOS logging and VPN processes without leaving a persistent binary or opening a listening port.
  • The article advises organizations to treat credentials and certificates held by a compromised edge-management platform as compromised and rotate them, even after the platform is patched.

Technologies: firewall, vpn, web-server

Products: fortimanager, fortigate, fortios, apache-http-server, mod-md

Vendors: fortinet, apache-software-foundation, palo-alto-networks

Threat Actor Abuses Agentic AI Pentesting Framework to Target South Korean Financial Institutions — Should Read

A Chinese-speaking, financially motivated threat actor allegedly used the ARTEX agentic AI pentesting framework to automate reconnaissance and exploit SQL injection and authentication-bypass flaws in South Korean financial web applications, stealing PII for about 67,000 people. The incident shows that LLM-enabled offensive tooling can lower the barrier to large-scale intrusion and data theft.

  • Zscaler ThreatLabz reported that a recently active campaign used the open-source ARTEX agentic penetration-testing framework to target multiple South Korean financial institutions.
  • ThreatLabz assessed with moderate confidence that a financially motivated, Chinese-speaking threat actor exploited internet-facing customer inquiry portals and employee mobile-application backends.
  • The campaign, first observed in late September 2026, reportedly exfiltrated personally identifiable information for approximately 67,000 individuals, including names, phone numbers, annual income figures, and loan limits.
  • ARTEX was configured with DeepSeek v4.1-flash as its primary LLM backend and Zhipu AI GLM-5.3 and xAI Grok 4.6 for supplementary reasoning.
  • The article states that the attackers used Claude Code sessions to seek advice on selling stolen South Korean financial PII and locating Korean-language Telegram channels used to sell stolen data.

Technologies: remote-access, proxy, dlp

item.title: Active Cisco CVE-2026-76519 Exploitation, Danfoss Exposure, and DPRK IT Worker Disruption
item.content:encoded:
Window: 14 Oct 18:00 → 14 Oct 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

Cisco Warns of Active Attacks Exploiting New Critical Secure Email Gateway Vulnerability — Must Read

Cisco says attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-76519, a critical Cisco Secure Email Gateway flaw that can let unauthenticated email senders write files and execute commands as root. Organizations should immediately update Content Scanner Tools to version 25.3.0.5525 or later or upgrade to a fixed AsyncOS release, then check appliances for compromise.

  • Cisco reported active exploitation of CVE-2026-76519, a critical flaw in Cisco Secure Email Gateway that can allow an unauthenticated sender to write files to the appliance operating system through a crafted email attachment and potentially execute commands as root.
  • Only Cisco Secure Email Gateway appliances with File Reputation enabled and Content Scanner Tools earlier than version 25.3.0.5525 are affected; Secure Email and Web Manager and Secure Web Appliance are not affected.
  • Cisco said the issue is fixed by Content Scanner Tools version 25.3.0.5525 or later, which can be installed without an AsyncOS upgrade or restart, and by AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 or 16.5.0-780.
  • Administrators can check for attempted exploitation by running "grep \"System Security\" system_logs" on each cluster member, although Cisco cautioned that a clean result does not prove a device was not compromised.
  • Cisco recommends preserving forensic evidence and rebuilding compromised virtual appliances on a fixed release without importing prior configuration files, while physical-appliance customers should contact Cisco TAC.

Technologies: email-security

Products: cisco-secure-email-gateway, asyncos, content-scanner-tools, secure-email-cloud, secure-email-and-web-manager, secure-web-appliance

Vendors: cisco

Frostbitten in France: A Danfoss StoreView Internet Exposure Report — Must Read

Hundreds of French supermarkets were hit after Internet-exposed Danfoss StoreView refrigeration controllers were switched into defrost mode, with most exposed devices running outdated firmware vulnerable to known flaws. The incident highlights the risk of leaving operational technology directly reachable from the Internet; operators largely responded by taking controllers offline rather than patching them.

  • Attackers switched hundreds of French supermarket refrigerators into defrost mode on 11 October, causing spoiled food and, in some cases, fires.
  • The incident involved Internet-exposed Danfoss StoreView refrigeration-controller management interfaces, and Danfoss said most affected controllers were unsupported older models or newer models running outdated firmware.
  • Danfoss patched CVE-2025-41450, which allowed administrator login using a code derived from the current date, in version 4.2, while versions 4.3.1 and later fixed CVE-2025-41451 and CVE-2025-41452 as well.
  • Censys observed exposed StoreView hosts in France decline from 1,825 on 11 October to 537 on 14 October, while patched and unpatched devices disappeared at roughly the same rate.
  • CERT-FR issued an emergency alert calling for Danfoss controllers to be immediately removed from the Internet.

Technologies: ics-scada, iot-device

Products: danfoss-storeview, ak-sm-800a

Vendors: danfoss

FBI raids DPRK IT worker laptop farms in Texas, US nationals arrested — Should Read

The FBI’s Texas-based Operation Lonestar Roundup seized about 187 laptops from North Korean Famous Chollima IT-worker laptop farms and led to arrests and charges against facilitators. The schemes used stolen or fake identities and U.S.-hosted devices to help DPRK operatives obtain remote jobs and generate millions of dollars.

  • The U.S. Department of Justice said it disrupted the North Korean-linked Famous Chollima IT-worker operation through arrests, charges, and the seizure of nearly 187 laptops.
  • During the Texas operation called Lonestar Roundup, the FBI searched 40 residences suspected of hosting laptop farms between September 21 and 25.
  • The laptop farms housed employer-issued computers that North Korean workers could access remotely to appear to be working from the United States.
  • An Ohio indictment described a scheme operating from 2019 through July 2025 that affected 70 U.S. companies and generated about $3 million for North Korean actors.
  • Authorities arrested U.S. nationals Michael James Bostelle and Juan Cecilio Pena Carrillo and separately charged 12 Chinese defendants in related cases.

North Macedonian police arrest alleged administrator behind OLVX cybercrime market — Should Read

North Macedonian police and the FBI arrested the alleged administrator of OLVX, a cybercrime marketplace accused of selling stolen personal data and credentials through more than 1,500 seller accounts between 2023 and 2025.

  • North Macedonian police and the FBI arrested the alleged administrator of the OLVX cybercrime marketplace after raiding his home in Golema Rečica.
  • The FBI said OLVX operated from 2023 to 2025 and allegedly sold personally identifiable information and login credentials through more than 1,500 seller accounts.
  • North Macedonia’s Interior Ministry said the suspect also ran a Telegram group called ONEMILI that offered tools for fraudulent refund schemes and other scams.

Products: telegram

Brooklyn DA’s office disrupts crypto scam targeting Russian community — May Read

The Brooklyn District Attorney’s Office and FBI seized 241 domains and 112 servers linked to a cryptocurrency investment scam that targeted Russian-speaking Brooklyn residents and stole millions. The operation also uncovered a follow-up recovery scam designed to defraud victims a second time.

  • The Brooklyn District Attorney’s Office and the FBI seized or disrupted 241 web domains and 112 servers used in a cryptocurrency investment scam targeting Russian-speaking people in Brooklyn.
  • Victims responded to Russian-language Facebook advertisements, were guided to create cryptocurrency accounts and transfer funds, then were blocked from withdrawing money unless they paid additional fees and taxes.
  • Authorities said victims likely lost millions of dollars, while approximately $300,000 in stolen funds was recovered.
  • Investigators found that the seized infrastructure included systems in Ukraine and other Eastern European countries and contained victim data, website data, and operational software.
  • The seized data indicated that the scammers also contacted victims after the initial fraud to offer false cryptocurrency recovery services for a fee.

OpenAI Dot Security Risks: What Admins Need to Know — Optional

OpenAI’s persistent Dot agent can access connected email, chat, code repositories, files, and a cloud computer, making prompt injection or agent misbehavior capable of turning one compromised instruction into broad data exposure or unauthorized actions. Organizations should treat Dots as privileged identities, minimize connectors and permissions, enforce human review, and contain blast radius by default.

  • OpenAI’s Dot is a persistent GPT-6 Astra agent with a dedicated cloud computer that can work across conversations and use connected applications such as email, files, calendars, chat, and code repositories.
  • The article reports that Dot can summarize or locate sensitive information available to its owner, potentially reducing the effort required to find overshared data in connected services.
  • OpenAI reports an 8.5% prompt-injection attack success rate for GPT-6 Astra in an external arena covering coding, tool-use, and computer-use scenarios.
  • Dot has tools that can search and send Slack messages, read Gmail and Google Drive content, modify GitHub repositories, access hosting-related resources, and send messages to its owner.
  • The article recommends minimizing connected applications, using scoped identities, writing restrictive custom rules, verifying unsolicited Dot messages through another channel, and treating Dots as privileged identities.

Technologies: browser, operating-system, source-control, cloud-platform

Products: openai-dot, gpt-6-astra, chatgpt, codex, chrome, debian, slack, microsoft-teams, github, gmail, google-drive

Vendors: openai, google, microsoft, github

The Threat Hunting Flywheel: Why Threat Hunting Isn’t About Finding Bad Things — Optional

Threat hunting is a continuous-improvement cycle, not merely a way to find active incidents: each investigation should strengthen detections, baselines, visibility, and future hunting hypotheses. Even hunts that find no threat provide valuable validation and identify gaps to fix.

  • The goal of threat hunting is to continuously improve a security program and reduce the likelihood of future harmful activity, not simply to find current incidents.
  • Threat hunters can focus their work through educated guesses, mapping normal activity, statistical analysis tools such as RITA, or machine-learning models that identify unusual events.
  • Investigations are iterative, beginning broadly and narrowing by filtering known-good activity while following relevant connections across system records.
  • A hunt that finds no threat can still validate defenses or reveal missing or misconfigured detections that need to be fixed.
  • Lessons from each hunt can be used to create detection rules, document normal behavior, close visibility gaps, share knowledge, and develop new hunting hypotheses.

Five Key Takeaways from Health-ISAC’s Executive Forum – Chicago — Optional

Health-ISAC’s Chicago Executive Forum highlighted that rapid AI adoption, autonomous agents, and legacy medical devices are eroding traditional security controls, making identity and authorization the central challenge. Health-sector leaders must maintain clear visibility into who or what is acting across their networks and retain the ability to stop unsafe actions.

  • Health-ISAC’s Chicago Executive Forum focused on AI governance, identity, legacy medical devices, and autonomous agents.
  • The article identifies the central cybersecurity question as who or what is taking action across a network and whether that action can still be stopped.
  • Peer discussions at the forum indicated that traditional controls are breaking down under the speed of AI adoption.

Cisco patches new Secure Email Gateway zero-day exploited in attacks — Must Read

Cisco patched CVE-2026-76519, an actively exploited Secure Email Gateway flaw that lets unauthenticated attackers send a malicious attachment to gain root-level command execution. Affected organizations should upgrade Content Scanner Tools to a fixed release and investigate devices for Cisco’s compromise indicators.

  • Cisco patched CVE-2026-76519, an actively exploited flaw in Secure Email Gateway that can let remote unauthenticated attackers execute commands with root privileges.
  • The flaw is a relative path traversal issue in the Advanced Malware Protection feature that can be triggered by an email containing a maliciously crafted attachment.
  • Affected Secure Email Gateway instances have File Reputation enabled and assigned to a mail policy and run Content Scanner Tools earlier than version 25.3.0.5525.
  • Cisco has deployed mitigations to cloud instances and contacted Cisco Secure Email Cloud device owners where it found evidence of a potential compromise.
  • Cisco advises affected customers to upgrade to a fixed release, review network and firewall logs, and renew credentials and cryptographic materials when possible.

Technologies: email-security

Ledger asks sellers across Asia to halt sales after supply-chain attack — Should Read

Ledger has halted reseller sales across Southeast Asia and Hong Kong after discovering modified hardware wallets from CryptoBilis that secretly captured 24-word recovery phrases and transmitted them over LTE, enabling cryptocurrency theft. The incident has also prompted reports involving other sellers and led Trezor to tighten its reseller network.

  • Ledger asked distributors and resellers in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to stop selling its wallets while it investigates hardware implant incidents.
  • Ledger confirmed that some wallets sold by CryptoBilis had been modified with a component that captured 24-word recovery phrases and transmitted them over LTE using a provisioned eSIM.
  • Ledger said the added component does not alter the Secure Element, Ledger operating system, transactions, or signatures, so its integrity self-checks do not detect it.
  • MediaMarkt removed Ledger products from its shelves after reports of modified devices purchased through the retailer, while Ledger said confirmed losses involve CryptoBilis devices.
  • Trezor said it found no evidence that its devices were compromised but will reduce its reseller network and revoke affected reseller authorizations on January 1, 2027.

Polish prosecutors say NSO Group retained technical access to Pegasus infrastructure used by the former government, potentially exposing surveillance data on opposition figures and other citizens to systems outside Poland. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the operation a major state scandal, though investigators have not confirmed NSO accessed specific intercepted materials.

  • Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office said an Internal Security Agency analysis found that the Central Anti-Corruption Bureau did not have full control over the Pegasus system operated by NSO Group.
  • Polish prosecutors said the server component used to infect mobile devices remained exclusively controlled by the manufacturer, while the Central Anti-Corruption Bureau lacked passwords for many administrative accounts.
  • Investigators found that data collected through the spyware was transmitted outside Poland through an anonymizing network using foreign servers and IP addresses.
  • Prosecutors said NSO Group had technical access to information from surveillance operations, but could not determine whether it actually accessed material from specific operations.

The U.S. charged 14 people and dismantled more than 40 Texas laptop farms used to help North Korean IT workers fraudulently obtain remote jobs at over 70 U.S. companies, generating roughly $3 million for the DPRK. The FBI warns the operation is expanding through subcontractors, stolen identities, and coercion, including targeting defense-related roles.

  • The U.S. Department of Justice charged 14 people and seized about 187 computers in connection with a North Korean remote IT worker scheme that affected more than 70 U.S. companies.
  • Authorities dismantled more than 40 laptop farms in Texas that hosted company-issued devices and helped overseas workers appear to be U.S.-based employees.

Microsoft fixes VPN issues caused by September Windows updates — Should Read

Microsoft fixed an Always On VPN bug caused by September 2026 Windows 11 updates that could leave connections stuck or fail after an initial attempt. Organizations should install KB5127648 or KB5127646, or temporarily force VPN profiles to use only SSTP or IKEv2.

  • Microsoft released KB5127648 and KB5127646 to fix Always On VPN connection issues caused by the September 2026 Windows 11 security updates.
  • The issue affected Windows 11 24H2 and later systems when automatic protocol selection or fallback was used and an initial VPN connection attempt failed.

IBM’s Cost of a Data Breach Report 2026: AI Is Now the Attacker and the Target — Optional

IBM’s 2026 Cost of a Data Breach Report finds that AI-driven and shadow-AI incidents are rising sharply, largely because organizations lack effective access controls and governance around AI systems and their data connections. Extensive use of security AI and automation can substantially reduce breach costs and response time.

  • IBM’s 2026 Cost of a Data Breach Report found that the global average cost of a data breach reached $4.99 million, a 12% increase from the previous year.
  • AI-driven attacks increased by 56%, and deepfake impersonation and AI-generated malware added an average of $1 million per breach.
  • Among organizations reporting an AI-related breach, 92% lacked proper AI access controls, while only 40% reported using access controls on AI models and data.

Be the Architect: Intentional AI Engagement for Cybersecurity Engineering — Optional

SpecterOps reports that a human-led, deliberately routed AI-agent workflow enabled one maintainer to modernize Ghostwriter’s 99-screen interface for $815.50 in model spend. The key lesson is to retain human ownership of problem framing, decisions, and verification while assigning agents bounded implementation, investigation, and QA tasks at appropriate capability and cost tiers.

  • Its AI Engagement Model uses a recurring workflow of framing the problem, challenging assumptions, verifying results, deciding on a direction, and then producing the implementation.

The Blind Spots of Agentic Pentesting and How to Close Them — Optional

Agentic pentesting can identify realistic exploit chains quickly but cannot safely or reliably cover unreachable assets or vulnerabilities lacking public exploits. The sponsored article argues that combining deterministic testing, agentic pentesting, breach-and-attack simulation, and exposure validation provides broader CVE coverage.

CISA warns admins to immediately fix Ivanti flaw exploited as zero-day — Must Read

CISA urges organizations to immediately patch Ivanti Connect Secure for CVE-2026-104935, a high-severity zero-day authentication bypass actively exploited to enable unauthenticated command execution, credential theft, and data exfiltration. Suspected compromises require forensic investigation and may warrant a factory reset, upgrade, and credential rotation.

  • CISA urged organizations to immediately patch CVE-2026-104935, an actively exploited Ivanti Connect Secure authentication-bypass flaw that enables unauthenticated remote command execution.
  • Ivanti released Connect Secure versions 22.8R2.5, 25.1.3.0, 25.1.3.1, and 25.1.1.2 to address the flaw and said exploitation in the wild is limited.
  • Volexity reported that threat actor UTA0576 chained the authentication bypass with remote code execution and privilege escalation flaws to obtain unauthenticated root-level code execution.
  • CISA said attackers have used the zero-day to steal credentials and exfiltrate data, while Volexity observed targeting of Active Directory secrets including LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys.
  • CISA advised organizations that find a compromised appliance to back up its configuration, factory-reset and update it, restore the configuration, and reset credentials, certificates, API keys, and license-server credentials.

Technologies: vpn, remote-access

Products: ivanti-connect-secure, integrity-checker-tool

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-103849) Adobe Commerce Template Injection Remote Code Execution — Must Read

Adobe has patched CVE-2026-103849, a critical unauthenticated template-injection flaw (CVSS 10.0) that allows remote code execution in Adobe Commerce, Adobe Commerce B2B, and Magento Open Source. Organizations should urgently update every production and staging storefront to the October 2026 dated releases, as external scans cannot reliably distinguish patched from vulnerable builds.

  • CVE-2026-103849 is a CVSS 10.0 template-injection flaw that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution in Adobe Commerce, Adobe Commerce B2B, and Magento Open Source.
  • Adobe released fixes in security bulletin APSB26-153 on 13 October 2026, with affected organizations instructed to install the October 2026 dated releases for their product line.
  • A store’s major version alone cannot establish whether it is vulnerable, because the dated September builds are affected while the corresponding October builds are fixed.
  • CyCognito found that roughly one in six observed storefronts had staging, test, QA, or demo markers, and these internet-facing environments may run the same codebase as production.
  • The article recommends inventorying all production and non-production instances, checking payment and checkout pages for unauthorized scripts, and reviewing admin accounts, API keys, and integration tokens for unexpected changes.

Products: adobe-commerce, adobe-commerce-b2b, magento-open-source, cycognito-platform

A global law-enforcement operation disrupted YAM Store and associated phishing kits CoGUI and Iron Man, which facilitated more than a billion phishing messages targeting organizations worldwide. Microsoft disabled over 20,000 linked accounts and blocked 100,000 fraudulent domains used to impersonate organizations and steal credentials and payment data.

curl Patches HTTP/2 Upload Flaw After PoC Demonstrates Client-Side Code Execution — Should Read

curl and libcurl 8.12.0–8.22.0 contain a high-severity HTTP/2 upload use-after-free flaw (CVE-2026-92392) that a malicious upload server could potentially turn into client-side code execution. Upgrade to curl 8.23.0 or a listed backported release, or disable HTTP/2 until patched.

  • curl fixed CVE-2026-92392 in version 8.23.0, a high-severity use-after-free flaw affecting curl and libcurl versions 8.12.0 through 8.22.0.

Its key advance is replacing legitimate Indonesian banking apps with tampered copies that bypass in-app signature, accessibility, screen-capture, and Play Integrity checks.

The group uses malicious documents, PowerShell downloaders, GitHub-hosted payloads, and a WinRAR exploit to deploy reverse shells and maintain access.

  • Cisco Talos and Recorded Future identified UAT-6275, also tracked as TAG-193, targeting government organizations across Central Asia and the wider Commonwealth of Independent States.

A U.S. congressional investigation found that Match Group failed to adequately prevent scammers from reaching users on Tinder and Hinge, with roughly 1.5 million bad actors matching with legitimate users in the first nine months of 2025. The report says outdated fraud-detection models and platform incentives amplified scammer visibility, while Match Group disputes aspects of the findings and cites newer biometric verification measures.

  • A U.S. Joint Economic Committee investigation found that nearly 1.5 million scammers and other bad actors on Tinder and Hinge matched with legitimate users during the first nine months of 2025.
  • The report said the median Tinder scammer's profile views increased by more than 700% from May 2024 to December 2025 and alleged that Tinder was more likely to show scammer or bad-actor profiles than regular-user profiles.
  • Investigators said internal Match Group documents showed that Tinder had not updated certain machine-learning models used to identify scammers for years, although a company official disputed that characterization.

Microsoft says recent Windows 11 updates can cause Remote Desktop connections to fail with error 0xC000000D on enterprise-managed hosts when Administrator protection is enabled. Until a fix is released, IT administrators should disable Administrator protection through policy management.

  • Microsoft says non-admin users may be unable to connect through Remote Desktop after recent Windows updates when Administrator protection is enabled.
  • Remote Desktop connections can fail with error 0xC000000D and the message "The token that was passed to the function is invalid."
  • The issue primarily affects enterprise-managed remote devices used as Remote Desktop hosts on Windows 11 24H2, 25H2, 26H1, and 26H2.
  • Microsoft says Administrator protection is enabled by default in Windows 11 security baselines for versions 24H2, 25H2, and 26H2 unless an organization changed the policy.

The Sign-In Link Pointed Home, and Home Was a Decoy — May Read

A phishing email used a legitimate Microsoft OAuth authorization endpoint and a fake, readable URL pointing to the victim’s own nonexistent subdomain to make the link appear trustworthy. Defenders should assess and hunt the OAuth client ID and app registration rather than trust URL-shaped query parameters such as uri.

  • A Teams-styled phishing email targeting a senior finance leader at a UK medical-device and infection-prevention manufacturer linked to the genuine Microsoft OAuth authorization endpoint.
  • The authorization link contained an unknown third-party OAuth client ID, prompt=none, identity and Microsoft Graph User.Read permissions, and a double-encoded uri parameter pointing to a nonexistent subdomain of the victim’s company.
  • The link omitted redirect_uri and response_type, which Microsoft documents as required parameters, while uri is not a documented Microsoft authorization parameter.
  • Microsoft filtering delivered the message despite passed SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and composite authentication checks and clean reputations for its Microsoft-hosted links.
  • IRONSCALES classified the email as VIP impersonation with 85 confidence and automatically quarantined the single affected mailbox, with no evidence that anyone clicked.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, email-security

Products: microsoft-entra-id, microsoft-teams, microsoft-graph, google-workspace, ironscales-themis

Vendors: microsoft, google, ironscales

Russian travel booking platform suspends reservations after cyberattack — May Read

Russian online travel agency Anywayanyday suspended new airline, train, and hotel bookings after a cyberattack disrupted its IT infrastructure, though it says existing reservations remain valid and there is no evidence of customer data compromise.

AI-Found Linux Kernel Flaw Gives Local Users Root, and Can Break a Guest Out to the Host — Should Read

CVE-2026-74580 (Vghost) is a Linux vhost flaw that can let local users gain root and, in certain virtualized configurations, allow a guest VM to compromise its host’s QEMU process. Organizations should install patched kernels and restrict access to /dev/vhost-net and /dev/vhost-vsock until patching is complete.

  • CVE-2026-74580, called Vghost, is a flaw in Linux’s vhost subsystem that can allow a local user to read and write kernel memory and gain root privileges.
  • In certain virtual-machine configurations using a virtual IOMMU and device-IOTLB mode, an untrusted guest can use the flaw to write outside intended memory in the host’s QEMU process.
  • The issue affects Linux kernels from version 4.11 through 7.2-rc4 and was reproduced on Ubuntu, RHEL, Amazon Linux, Microsoft Azure Linux, and Oracle Linux.
  • The upstream fix clears vhost’s memory-mapping cache whenever a virtual ring is reconfigured, and organizations should install a kernel containing commit de845981da67 and reboot.
  • Until systems are patched, the article recommends restricting access to /dev/vhost-net and /dev/vhost-vsock; only a patched kernel addresses the guest-to-host path.

Socket CISO Andrew Becherer says security founders win buyers by addressing immediate, concrete pain and honestly acknowledging gaps, rather than selling distant hypotheticals. He also cautions that AI-built security tools create lasting maintenance and reliability responsibilities.

Picus argues that agentic pentesting can uncover realistic exploit chains but cannot safely or consistently test all assets or vulnerabilities, especially unreachable systems and CVEs lacking public exploits. It promotes combining deterministic testing, agentic pentesting, exposure validation, and breach-and-attack simulation to prioritize exploitable exposures faster.

  • Agentic pentesting can produce varying results between runs and may be costly and slow at large organizations, while deterministic automated testing is presented as faster, less expensive, and repeatable.
  • Because it relies on safely running real attacks, agentic pentesting cannot test assets that are unreachable or too risky to target, such as segmented, air-gapped, or fragile production systems.
  • In the nginx-ui CVE-2026-33032 example, agentic pentesting tested 120 of 480 affected instances, confirming 80 as exploitable and finding 40 blocked, while 360 instances remained untested.

OpenAI engineer arrested for allegedly planting spy device in office — Should Read

A former OpenAI engineer was arrested after allegedly hiding encrypted audio-recording devices in executive conference rooms at the company’s San Francisco offices to capture confidential discussions. OpenAI said it fired the employee, referred the case to the FBI, and found no evidence that model weights, source code, or customer data were accessed or exfiltrated.

  • The U.S. Department of Justice announced that Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national who had worked at OpenAI since July 2025, was arrested on October 9 and charged with illegally intercepting oral communications.
  • OpenAI security personnel found a concealed recording device plugged into a USB port behind a television in an executive conference room on September 30.
  • The DOJ alleges that the device was installed around September 28, held encrypted data, and was concealed in toilet paper.
  • OpenAI said it terminated Alfozan and referred the incident to the FBI after using its AI models to help identify the employee allegedly responsible.
  • OpenAI stated that it had no indication that model weights, source code, or customer data had been accessed or removed.

Vendors: openai

The Noise Inside the Network: How an Unsophisticated Attack Exposed a Third-Party Risk — May Read

A European bank was compromised through a misconfigured third-party gateway and stolen credentials, enabling months of noisy network reconnaissance and password guessing. Cortex XDR stopped an attempted WSUS-based escalation, underscoring that MFA, prompt patching, and strong third-party access controls can prevent major incidents.

  • A European bank detected unauthorized VPN-based access attempts that had occurred over several months and engaged Unit 42 to investigate the intrusion.
  • The intrusion began through a third-party-managed external gateway appliance that was not configured to enforce strict authentication, using compromised credentials.
  • After entering the network, the attacker conducted broad scans, tested passwords against administrator accounts, and accessed internal documentation and data shares.
  • The attacker attempted to exploit a Windows Server Update Services remote-code-execution vulnerability on the bank’s central configuration management server.
  • Cortex XDR detected and contained the unauthorized code-execution attempt, and Unit 42’s subsequent forensic review found no additional attacker presence or persistent backdoors.
